To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified and characterized expressed V, D and J genes in ferrets.
The domestic ferret ( Mustela putorious furo ) is an important animal model for human respiratory disease.
we have characterized the ferret TRBV locus by identifying expressed V, D and J genes and have curated the locus to include all expressed and non-expressed genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the expressed V, (D), and J genes of the TRB locus in the ferret.
the characterization of the ferret locus and the annotation of expressed V, D, and J genes.
the identification and characterization of expressed V, D and J gene segments in ferrets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ferret TRBV genes are most similar to those of the dog and the human TRBD and TRBJ genes are most similar those of the dog.
the ferret TRBV gene repertoire is similar to that of dog.
the ferret TRBV genes are most similar to dog TRBV genes, and the ferret TRBJ and TRBD genes are most similar in structure to cat TRBJ and TRBJ genes, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ferret TR locus is similar to other mammals, and that the ferret V, D, and J gene repertoires are similar to that of humans and dogs, with a few exceptions.
we have identified 27 expressed V genes, 2 D genes, 2 J genes, and 3 C genes.
we have characterized the TRB locus in ferrets and provided an updated annotation of the expressed TRB genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ferret TRBV genes are organized in 11 families (1–11) that are very similar to those of other mammals.
the ferret TR locus is well suited for detailed studies of the ferret TCR repertoires.
we now have a complete picture of the ferret locus and can use this information to study the diversity of the TRB repertoire in this species.
